text: Restart your phone regularly to clear app caching and memory glitches.
explanation: Regular restarts clear accumulated issues like runaway caching, network connectivity problems, and memory leaks without requiring any deletions or configuration changes.

text: Enable Auto-Archive for unused Android apps to free space automatically.
explanation: Google Play's Auto Archive feature removes unused app data while keeping icons on your home screen, so you can restore apps anytime without losing them completely.

text: Use hibernation mode instead of sleep for extended laptop breaks.
explanation: Hibernation saves your work and shuts down the laptop while using almost no power, making it ideal for breaks longer than an hour.

text: Calibrate your laptop battery every 2-3 months for accurate reporting.
explanation: Battery calibration involves a full discharge and recharge cycle that helps the battery reporting system maintain accuracy and optimal performance.

text: Set your screen to turn off after 1-2 minutes of inactivity.
explanation: The display is one of the biggest power consumers—automatically turning it off during short breaks saves substantial energy throughout the day.

text: Check battery health reports monthly to catch issues early.
explanation: Regular battery diagnostics let you monitor capacity degradation and plan replacements before catastrophic failure disrupts your work.

text: Think twice before upgrading—do you really need a new device?
explanation: Extending your current device's life by even one year prevents the mining of rare earth minerals and significantly reduces e-waste generation.

text: Take broken electronics to a repair cafe instead of replacing them.
explanation: Community repair cafes offer free fixes by volunteers, helping you avoid the environmental cost of mining new materials and manufacturing replacements.

text: Check if manufacturers offer take-back programs for old devices.
explanation: Many brands now accept old products for recycling or credit, ensuring proper material recovery that's more efficient than generic recycling facilities.

text: Never throw electronics in regular trash—find certified e-waste recyclers.
explanation: E-waste contains toxic substances like lead and mercury that leach into soil and water from landfills, harming ecosystems and human health.

text: Choose devices with modular, repairable designs when buying new.
explanation: Modular electronics let you upgrade or replace individual components instead of discarding entire devices, dramatically extending product lifespan.

text: Demand products designed for recyclability from manufacturers.
explanation: Consumer pressure for recyclable electronics forces manufacturers to adopt sustainable design practices and phase out products with planned obsolescence.

text: Remember your old phone contains precious metals—recycle to recover them.
explanation: Electronic devices contain gold, silver, copper, and cobalt. Recycling recovers these materials, reducing the need for destructive new mining operations.

text: Unplug fully charged devices to avoid unnecessary heat buildup.
explanation: Leaving devices plugged in after reaching 100% generates heat that degrades battery health and wastes standby power over time.

text: Don't leave laptops plugged in constantly—use battery power occasionally.
explanation: Always being plugged in stresses the battery by keeping it at 100% charge continuously, which reduces its long-term capacity and lifespan.

text: Close apps running in background that you're not actively using.
explanation: Background applications consume CPU cycles and RAM even when idle, continuously draining battery power without providing value.

text: Choose brands that publish transparent sustainability reports.
explanation: Transparency signals genuine commitment to reducing emissions, using better materials, ensuring fair labor practices, and taking environmental responsibility.
